people_spec: Founder & CEO (Clint Zhang) — owns the roadmap and is the de-facto technical decision maker; there is no CTO or VP Engineering at this company
Chief Engineer — the title Remarcable's own engineer postings name as the reporting line ('Reporting directly to the Chief Engineer'); this is the person who owns delivery today
Engineering Team Lead — listed as the top engineering node on Remarcable's public org chart
Head of Product / Director of Product — co-owner of the cycle-time problem the Product Manager req describes
talk_track: I spent fourteen years building software for contractors — Xactimate at Verisk, then JobNimbus — and last year I took one engineering org from a 42-hour cycle time to under 20 while automating releases end to end. Your Senior DevOps req asks a single hire to "take ownership of our cloud infrastructure, CI/CD systems, system reliability, observability, and scalability," plus SOC 2 evidence collection. Here is the read worth having either way: when all five land on one requisition, nobody owns delivery speed today, and that hire will spend two quarters on reliability and audit work while cycle time sits exactly where it is. The cheaper sequence is to instrument cycle time and release lead time first — in trade-vertical SaaS the queue is almost always in review and QA, not infrastructure — and then hire against the number instead of the title. Worth measuring before that person starts? — Bill Bowers
